questions.text_english: Which country was the most affected by the potato famine during 1845 – 1849 ?
questions.solution: Ireland (आयरलैंड) was the most affected country during the potato famine of 1845–1849. The Irish population was heavily dependent on potato as their primary food crop. When a water mould destroyed potato harvests across Ireland, it led to mass starvation and death of nearly one million people and forced emigration of another million. France, USA, and Sweden did not experience potato famine on this devastating scale.

questions.text_english:
Arrange the following historical events in chronological order and choose the correct option :
I. Publication of Bengal Gazette
II. Publication of Diamond Sutra
III. Publication of Bible by Johann Gutenberg
IV. Return of Marco Polo to Italy from China
questions.solution: The correct chronological order is II, IV, III, I. The Diamond Sutra was printed in China in 868 AD, making it the world's oldest printed book. Marco Polo returned to Italy from China around 1295 AD. Johann Gutenberg printed the Bible around 1448 AD using the printing press. Bengal Gazette was the first Indian newspaper published by James Augustus Hicky in 1780 AD. Therefore, option D (II, IV, III, I) is correct.

questions.text_english:
Two statements labelled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given below. Read both the statements carefully and choose the correct option :
Assertion (A) : Giuseppe Mazzini was a revolutionary from Italy.
Reason (R) : He founded underground organisations.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both the Assertion and the Reason are correct, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Giuseppe Mazzini was indeed a revolutionary from Italy who believed in the unification of Italy. He founded two secret revolutionary organisations — Young Italy in Marseilles and Young Europe in Berne — through which he spread nationalist ideas. His founding of underground organisations is what made him a revolutionary, so the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Hence, option A is correct.

questions.text_english: Between which two leaders was the Poona Pact signed in 1932 ?
questions.solution: The Poona Pact was signed in September 1932 between Bhimrao Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi. When the British announced separate electorates for the depressed classes (Dalits), Gandhi went on a fast unto death opposing it. Ambedkar then negotiated with Gandhi, and the Poona Pact was reached, giving reserved seats for the depressed classes within the general electorate rather than separate electorates. Options B, C, and D are incorrect as Nehru, Lord Irwin, and Jinnah were not part of this pact.

questions.solution: The picture represents Germania, the female allegory of the German nation. Germania was depicted as a strong, armoured woman wearing a crown of oak leaves (symbolising German heroism) and carrying a sword. She was used as a symbol of German nationalism during the unification of Germany in the 19th century. Marianne represents France, Britannia represents Britain, and Columbia represents America. The visual characteristics of the figure — the armour, the sword, and the setting — are consistent with depictions of Germania.

questions.text: सोलहवीं शताब्दी के मध्य में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी घातक बीमारी पुर्तगाल और स्पेन से अमेरिका में फैली थी ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following deadly disease spread in America through Portugal and Spain in mid-sixteenth century ?
questions.solution: Smallpox (चेचक) was the deadly disease that spread in America through Portuguese and Spanish colonisers in the mid-sixteenth century. The native American populations had no immunity against smallpox as it was a disease unknown to them. It wiped out entire communities and civilisations like the Aztecs and Incas, making conquest much easier for the Europeans. Yellow fever, malaria, and cholera did not have the same devastating impact on native Americans at that time.

sub_questions.text_english: Analyse the role of language in the development of nationalism in Poland during the nineteenth century.

key_points: Polish language was suppressed by Russian rulers after the partition of Poland
Language became a tool of resistance and national identity
Church used Polish language to keep national identity alive

sub_questions.solution: After Poland was partitioned and taken over by Russia, the Russian language was imposed on Polish people in schools and public life. Polish language was forbidden in official and educational spaces. However, the Polish language became a powerful symbol of national identity and resistance. The Catholic Church used Polish in its religious activities, keeping the language alive among the people. When Russian authorities forced Russian-language instruction in schools, Polish children refused to answer in Russian and resisted oppression. Thus, language became a means of national solidarity and a tool of resistance against foreign domination, strengthening Polish nationalism throughout the nineteenth century.

sub_questions.text: 1815 की वियना संधि के मुख्य प्रावधानों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Analyse the main provisions of the Treaty of Vienna of 1815.

key_points: Restoration of conservative regimes and monarchies overthrown by Napoleon
Redrawing of European boundaries to contain France
Establishment of a new conservative order in Europe

sub_questions.solution: The Treaty of Vienna (1815) was drawn up by conservative powers — Britain, Russia, Prussia, and Austria — after Napoleon's defeat. Its main provisions included: first, the restoration of dynasties that had been overthrown by Napoleon, thus reinstating the old monarchical order. Second, European boundaries were redrawn to reduce France's power and prevent future expansion. Third, France was surrounded by stronger neighbouring states. Fourth, the conservative order was reinforced by suppressing liberal and nationalist movements. The treaty aimed to establish stability in Europe based on the principle of legitimacy, though it ignored the aspirations of liberal nationalists.

sub_questions.text_english: "Women played an important role during the Civil Disobedience Movement." Support the statement with appropriate arguments.

key_points: Women participated in large numbers in marches and protests
They manufactured and sold salt in defiance of the salt laws
They picketed liquor and foreign cloth shops
They considered participation a sacred duty
Despite Gandhi's initial hesitation, women's participation was massive

sub_questions.solution: Women played a crucial and historically significant role during the Civil Disobedience Movement of 1930. When Mahatma Gandhi launched the Salt March, thousands of women came out of their homes to participate actively in political activities for the first time in large numbers. They participated in protest marches, manufactured salt illegally, and picketed shops selling foreign cloth and liquor. Women from urban areas as well as rural communities joined the movement, seeing it as a sacred national duty. High-caste women from respectable families, who had never stepped out publicly before, openly defied colonial laws. They were inspired by Gandhi's call and considered participation their national and moral obligation. Their involvement gave the movement a mass character and demonstrated that the struggle for independence had the support of the entire Indian society, cutting across gender barriers. Despite initially being discouraged by Gandhi himself, women's participation proved unstoppable and transformed the Civil Disobedience Movement into a truly people's movement.

sub_questions.text: "भारतीय लोक-कथाओं को पुनर्जीवित करने से भारत में राष्ट्रवाद सुदृढ़ हुआ।" उपयुक्त तर्कों सहित इस कथन की पुष्टि कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: "The revival of Indian folklore strengthened nationalism in India." Support the statement with appropriate arguments.

key_points: Folk songs and tales preserved a sense of national identity
Nationalists collected and popularised folk traditions
Tagore collected folk songs to revive Bengali identity
Local tales helped people connect with their cultural roots
Revival countered colonial claim that India had no culture

sub_questions.solution: The revival of Indian folklore played an important role in strengthening nationalism in India during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. Nationalists believed that to build a strong national identity, India's ancient cultural and folk traditions needed to be rediscovered and celebrated. Rabindranath Tagore himself began collecting ballads and folk songs to revive the spirit of Bengali identity and culture. In many parts of India, folk tales and oral traditions helped people reconnect with their shared cultural heritage, creating a sense of common identity and solidarity. These stories spoke of brave heroes, cultural values, and a glorious past, which inspired people to take pride in their civilisation. By celebrating indigenous traditions, nationalists challenged the colonial argument that India was backward and uncivilised. The revival of folklore thus created cultural nationalism — a belief that the nation had a rich, unique heritage worth protecting and celebrating — which eventually merged with the political movement for independence.

1857 के विद्रोह के बाद प्रेस की स्वतंत्रता के प्रति औपनिवेशिक सरकार का रवैया बदल गया। कुद्ध अंग्रेजों ने 'देसी' प्रेस का मुँह बंद करने की माँग की। ज्यों-ज्यों भाषाई समाचार पत्र राष्ट्रवाद से समर्थन में मुखर होते गए, त्यों-त्यों औपनिवेशिक सरकार में कड़े नियंत्रण के प्रस्ताव पर बहस तेज़ होने लगी। आइरिश प्रेस कानून के तर्ज पर 1878 में वर्नाक्युलर प्रेस एक्ट लागू कर दिया गया। इससे सरकार को भाषाई प्रेस में छपी रपट और संपादकीय को सेंसर करने का व्यापक हक़ मिल गया। अब से सरकार ने विभिन्न प्रदेशों से छपने वाले भाषाई अख़बारों पर नियमित नज़र रखनी शुरू कर दी। अगर किसी रपट को बाग़ी करार दिया जाता था तो अख़बार को पहले चेतावनी दी जाती थी, और अगर चेतावनी की अनसुनी हुई, तो अख़बार को जब्त किया जा सकता था और छपाई की मशीनें छीन ली जा सकती थीं।

Read the given source carefully and answer the questions that follow :

Print and Censorship

After the revolt of 1857, the attitude of the colonial government towards freedom of the press changed. Enraged Englishmen demanded a clamp down on the 'native' press. As vernacular newspapers became assertively nationalist, the colonial government began debating measures of stringent control. In 1878, the Vernacular Press Act was passed, modelled on the Irish Press Laws. It provided the government with extensive rights to censor reports and editorials in the vernacular press. From now on the government kept regular track of the vernacular newspapers published in different provinces. When a report was judged as seditious, the newspaper was warned, and if the warning was ignored, the press was liable to be seized and the printing machinery confiscated.

sub_questions.solution: The colonial government was not in favour of freedom of the press because after the revolt of 1857, vernacular newspapers became increasingly nationalist and critical of British rule. These newspapers were spreading seditious ideas and mobilising public opinion against the colonial government, which posed a direct threat to British authority in India.

sub_questions.solution: The Vernacular Press Act gave the colonial government two important powers. First, it gave the government extensive rights to censor reports and editorials published in vernacular (Indian language) newspapers. Second, if a newspaper published a seditious report and ignored the government's warning, the government had the power to seize the newspaper and confiscate its printing machinery, effectively shutting it down.

questions.text_english: In which Indian state is 'Bamboo drip irrigation' system used ?
questions.solution: Bamboo drip irrigation is a traditional irrigation system used in Meghalaya. This ingenious system, practised by tribal communities of the state for over 200 years, uses bamboo pipes to divert and carry water from streams and springs to agricultural fields. It is not used in Himachal Pradesh, Kerala, or Rajasthan. This system is a remarkable example of traditional water harvesting knowledge that conserves water while irrigating crops efficiently.

First, it has established a network of National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, and Biosphere Reserves across the country to protect natural habitats and endangered species. Second, the Wildlife Protection Act was enacted in 1972, which provides legal protection to wildlife and prohibits hunting of many endangered species like tigers, elephants, and rhinoceros.

questions.text_english: Explain any three main factors responsible for land degradation.

key_points: Deforestation leads to soil erosion and land degradation
Overgrazing by cattle destroys vegetation and topsoil
Mining and industrial activities cause pollution and land damage

questions.solution: Land degradation refers to the decline in the quality and productivity of land. Three major factors responsible for it are: First, deforestation — clearing of forests for agriculture and development removes the protective vegetation cover, leading to soil erosion by wind and water and reducing the land's fertility. Second, overgrazing — excessive grazing by livestock destroys natural vegetation, leaving the soil bare and vulnerable to erosion and degradation. Third, mining and industrial activities — mining operations leave behind large pits and heaps of waste material, while industrial effluents and chemicals pollute the surrounding soil, making large areas unfit for cultivation and damaging the natural composition of land.

sub_questions.text: भारत में पटसन उद्योग अधिकांशत: पश्चिम बंगाल में अवस्थित होने के कारणों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the reasons why most of the Jute industries in India are located in West Bengal.

key_points: Proximity to raw material — jute is grown in abundance in West Bengal and neighbouring states
Availability of cheap labour from densely populated rural areas
River Hooghly provides water for processing jute
Kolkata port enables export of jute products
Well-developed transport and power supply in the region

sub_questions.solution: Most jute industries in India are concentrated in West Bengal due to several locational advantages. First, West Bengal and the adjoining areas of Bihar, Odisha, and Assam are the major jute-growing regions of India, providing easy and cheap access to raw material. Second, the Hugli river provides abundant water needed for retting and processing jute fibres. Third, cheap and abundant labour is available from the densely populated rural areas of West Bengal and Bihar. Fourth, the Kolkata port facilitates the easy export of finished jute goods to international markets. Fifth, well-developed transport infrastructure including railways and roadways connects the factories to markets and raw material areas. Sixth, the availability of coal from Jharkhand and power supply supports industrial operations. These combined factors have made West Bengal the dominant centre of India's jute industry.

sub_questions.text: औद्योगिक प्रदूषण को कम करने हेतु उपायों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the measures to reduce industrial pollution.

key_points: Minimising use of water through reuse and recycling
Treating hot water and effluents before releasing into rivers
Use of oil, gas and electricity instead of coal to reduce air pollution
Rainwater harvesting and ground water recharge
Regulatory measures by government — Environmental Protection Act

sub_questions.solution: Industrial pollution can be reduced through various measures. First, industries should minimise the use of water in manufacturing processes and reuse and recycle water wherever possible to reduce water pollution. Second, hot water and chemical effluents must be treated in effluent treatment plants before being discharged into rivers or land, preventing water and soil contamination. Third, industries should shift from coal-based energy to cleaner fuels like natural gas, oil, or renewable electricity to reduce air pollution. Fourth, tall chimneys should be fitted with electrostatic precipitators and scrubbers to reduce particulate matter and gaseous emissions. Fifth, the government must strictly enforce environmental laws like the Environment Protection Act and Water and Air Pollution Acts, and impose heavy penalties on violators. Sixth, rainwater harvesting should be promoted to reduce dependence on groundwater and rivers.

Read the following statements about the functions of political parties and choose the correct option :

options.B: केवल II, III और IV सही हैं।
options.C: केवल I, III और IV सही हैं।

options_english.B: Only II, III and IV are correct.

questions.solution: Statements I, II, and III are correct functions of political parties. Political parties build public opinion by raising and highlighting issues, play the role of the opposition by critiquing the government, and present their programmes and policies to the public during elections. Statement IV is incorrect because foreign policy is made by the government (the executive), not directly by political parties. Even the ruling party makes foreign policy through the government machinery, not as a party. Therefore, option A (Only I, II and III are correct) is the right answer.

questions.solution: The correct matching is: Union List — Defence (iv), State List — Police (i), Concurrent List — Adoption (iii), Residuary subjects — Computer software (ii). Defence is a Union List subject as national security is under Central Government. Police is a State List subject as law and order is a state matter. Adoption (family law) is a Concurrent List subject where both Centre and State can legislate. Computer software was not included in any list when the Constitution was drafted, so it falls under Residuary subjects which the Centre legislates on. Hence option C is correct.

options.A: सभी वर्गों की सत्ता में साझेदारी सुनिश्चित करना।
options.B: सिंहली को राज भाषा घोषित करना।
options.C: तमिल को राज भाषा घोषित करना।
options.D: सिंहलियों को सरकारी नौकरियों में प्राथमिकता की नीति लागू करना।

options_english.B: Declaring Sinhala as the official language.
options_english.C: Declaring Tamil as the official language.
options_english.D: Implementing a policy of preference for Sinhalese in government jobs.

questions.solution: The 1956 law in Sri Lanka declaring Sinhala as the sole official language gave rise to the possibility of civil war. This law was seen as majoritarian and discriminatory by the Tamil-speaking minority, which constituted about 18% of the population. Tamil leaders felt that the language policy undermined their identity and opportunities. This led to growing resentment, demand for autonomy, and eventually violent ethnic conflict. Option A would have prevented conflict; options C and D are not what the 1956 law contained.
questions.solution_hindi: 1956 के कानून में सिंहली को एकमात्र राजभाषा घोषित करने से श्रीलंका में गृहयुद्ध की संभावना उत्पन्न हुई। तमिल अल्पसंख्यकों ने इसे भेदभावपूर्ण माना जिससे जातीय संघर्ष शुरू हुआ।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा देश 'साथ आकर संघ बनाने' का उदाहरण है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following countries is an example of a 'coming together federation' ?
questions.solution: Australia is an example of a 'coming together federation'. In this type of federation, independent states come together voluntarily to form a larger union, pooling their sovereignty while retaining some degree of autonomy. The USA, Switzerland, and Australia are classic examples where independent states joined together to form a federation. India, Spain, and Belgium are examples of 'holding together federations' where a large country decides to divide power between the constituent states and the central authority. Hence, option D is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: ऑस्ट्रेलिया 'साथ आकर संघ बनाने' का उदाहरण है। इस प्रकार के संघ में स्वतंत्र राज्य स्वेच्छा से एकजुट होकर एक बड़ा संघ बनाते हैं। भारत, स्पेन और बेल्जियम 'साथ रहने वाले संघ' के उदाहरण हैं।

questions.text_english: Suggest any two reforms to strengthen 'party system' in India.

key_points: Internal democracy within parties — regular elections within the party
State funding of elections to reduce corrupt practices and money power

questions.solution: Two important reforms to strengthen the party system in India are: First, internal democracy should be practised within political parties, meaning parties should hold regular internal elections for their leadership positions so that leaders are accountable to party members rather than relying on dynastic or personal connections. Second, the state should fund elections to reduce the influence of money and corporate donations, which currently make parties dependent on rich donors and prone to corruption. These reforms would make parties more transparent, accountable, and representative.
questions.solution_hindi: दलीय व्यवस्था को मजबूत करने के दो उपाय: पहला, राजनीतिक दलों में आंतरिक लोकतंत्र स्थापित किया जाए और नियमित आंतरिक चुनाव हों। दूसरा, चुनावों में धन-बल को कम करने के लिए राज्य द्वारा चुनाव-वित्तपोषण की व्यवस्था की जाए।

questions.text: "शिकायतों का बने रहना लोकतंत्र की सफलता की गवाही देता है।" उदाहरणों सहित इस कथन की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: "Complaints are the testimony to the success of Democracy." Explain the statement with examples.

key_points: In a democracy, people have the freedom to raise complaints and criticise the government
The existence of complaints shows people are aware of their rights and the system is open enough to allow dissent

questions.solution: The statement means that in a democracy, the fact that people are free to complain about the government and its failures actually proves that democracy is working. In a dictatorship, people cannot voice grievances — they are silenced. But in a democracy, citizens freely criticise government policies, demand accountability, and expect better governance. For example, in India, people openly criticise corruption, demand better roads and hospitals, and hold protests. The right to complain reflects the freedom of speech and the presence of an accountable system, which are signs of a successful democracy.
questions.solution_hindi: इस कथन का अर्थ है कि लोकतंत्र में लोगों को शिकायत करने की स्वतंत्रता ही लोकतंत्र की सफलता का प्रमाण है। तानाशाही में लोग शिकायत नहीं कर सकते। भारत में लोग सरकार की नीतियों की आलोचना करते हैं जो लोकतंत्र की सफलता दर्शाता है।

questions.text: "भाषा के आधार पर प्रांतों का गठन भारत की लोकतांत्रिक राजनीति के लिए पहली और एक कठिन परीक्षा थी।" इस कथन की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: "The creation of linguistic states was the first and a major test for democratic politics in India." Explain the statement.

key_points: Many leaders feared linguistic states would lead to national disintegration
States Reorganisation Commission (1953) was set up to examine the demand
Andhra Pradesh was carved out in 1953 after Potti Sriramulu's death
Reorganisation of states on linguistic basis was completed by 1956
The reorganisation actually strengthened national unity rather than breaking India apart

questions.solution: The creation of linguistic states was considered the first and major test for democratic India because many national leaders, including Nehru, feared that reorganising states on the basis of language would weaken national unity and encourage separatism. However, the demand for linguistic states was very strong among people. In 1952, Potti Sriramulu went on a fast unto death demanding a separate Andhra state for Telugu speakers, and after his death, Andhra Pradesh was carved out in 1953. Following this, the States Reorganisation Commission was set up and in 1956, states were reorganised on linguistic lines. Contrary to fears, this process actually strengthened democratic India by making administration more accessible and creating states where people shared a common language and culture.
questions.solution_hindi: भाषाई आधार पर राज्यों के गठन को राष्ट्रीय नेताओं ने देश की एकता के लिए खतरनाक माना। 1952 में पोट्टी श्रीरामुलु के बलिदान के बाद आंध्र प्रदेश बना। 1956 में राज्य पुनर्गठन आयोग की सिफारिशों पर भाषाई आधार पर राज्य बने। यह लोकतंत्र की सफलता थी।

sub_questions.text_english: Compare the Belgian model and the Sri Lankan model of power sharing.

key_points: Belgium adopted accommodation and power sharing among Dutch, French, and German communities
Sri Lanka adopted majoritarianism, favouring the Sinhala majority
Belgium avoided civil war; Sri Lanka fell into ethnic conflict
Belgium's constitution gave equal representation to both Dutch and French speakers in Cabinet
Sri Lanka's 1956 law made Sinhala the only official language, alienating Tamils

sub_questions.solution: Belgium and Sri Lanka represent two contrasting approaches to managing ethnic diversity. Belgium, with Dutch, French, and German-speaking communities, adopted a policy of accommodation and power sharing. The Belgian Constitution ensures equal representation in the Central Government for both Dutch and French speakers. A separate government was created for each linguistic community, and Brussels has a separate government with equal representation. This model successfully prevented conflict and kept the country united. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, adopted majoritarianism where the Sinhala majority dominated political power. The 1956 law made Sinhala the only official language, marginalising Tamil speakers. Tamils were denied representation, which led to civil war that lasted for decades. Belgium's inclusive approach promoted unity while Sri Lanka's exclusionary policies generated violence and instability. Belgium is thus considered a success story of power sharing, while Sri Lanka is a cautionary tale.

sub_questions.text: लोकतंत्र में सत्ता की साझेदारी क्यों आवश्यक है ? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Why is power sharing necessary in a democracy ? Explain.

key_points: Reduces possibility of conflict between social groups
Ensures stability and political order in society
Reflects the spirit of democracy — people govern themselves
Prevents tyranny of the majority
Prudential reason — conflict avoidance; moral reason — inherently good

sub_questions.solution: Power sharing is necessary in a democracy for both prudential and moral reasons. The prudential reason is that sharing power helps reduce the possibility of conflict between different social groups. When one group monopolises power, other groups feel excluded and may resort to violence, threatening social stability. By distributing power, all groups get a stake in the system and are more likely to support it. The moral reason is that power sharing is the very essence of democracy — it reflects the principle that people should govern themselves. Concentrating power in one place is undemocratic and can lead to tyranny. Power sharing through federalism, separation of powers, coalition governments, and participation of social groups ensures that no single individual or group dominates, making governance more accountable, inclusive, and stable.

कितने राजनीतिक दल ?

कई देशों में सिर्फ एक ही दल को सरकार बनाने और चलाने की अनुमति है। इस कारण उन्हें एकदलीय शासन-व्यवस्था कहा जाता है। कुछ देशों में सत्ता आमतौर पर दो मुख्य दलों के बीच ही बदलती रहती है। वहाँ अनेक दूसरी पार्टियाँ हो सकती हैं, वे भी चुनाव लड़कर कुछ सीटें जीत सकती हैं पर सिर्फ दो ही दल बहुमत पाने और सरकार बनाने के प्रबल दावेदार होते हैं। इसे दो-दलीय व्यवस्था कहा जाता है। जब अनेक दल सत्ता के लिए होड़ में हों और दो दलों से ज़्यादा के लिए या तो अपने दम पर या दूसरों से गठबंधन करके सत्ता में आने का ठीक-ठाक अवसर हो तो इसे हम बहुदलीय व्यवस्था कहते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Read the given source carefully and answer the questions that follow :

How many political parties ?

In some countries, only one party is allowed to control and run the government. These are called one-party systems. In some countries, power usually changes between two main parties. Several other parties may exist, contest elections and win a few seats in the national legislatures. Such a party system is called two-party system. If several parties compete for power, and more than two parties have a reasonable chance of coming to power either on their own strength or in alliance with others, we call it a multiparty system.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the main feature of 'multi-party system'.

key_points: In a multiparty system, more than two parties have a reasonable chance of coming to power either on their own or in alliance with others.

sub_questions.solution: The main feature of a multiparty system is that several parties compete for power, and more than two parties have a reasonable chance of forming the government, either on their own strength or by forming coalitions with other parties. India is an example of a multiparty system where many national and regional parties compete for power.

sub_questions.text_english: Why is a 'one-party system' not compatible with democracy ?

key_points: A one-party system does not allow citizens a choice or the ability to replace the government through elections, which violates the basic principles of democracy.

sub_questions.solution: A one-party system is not compatible with democracy because democracy requires free and fair competition among multiple parties, giving citizens the right to choose their government and vote it out if it performs poorly. In a one-party system, citizens have no meaningful choice, there is no political competition, and the ruling party cannot be changed through elections — all of which contradict the fundamental principles of democratic governance.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the main characteristics of a coalition government.

key_points: Formed when no single party gets a majority
Two or more parties come together to form the government
Requires compromise and coordination among coalition partners

sub_questions.solution: A coalition government is formed when no single party wins an outright majority in elections. Its main characteristics are: First, it is formed by two or more political parties coming together to create a majority and run the government. Second, it requires constant negotiation, compromise, and coordination among the partner parties on policy decisions. Third, it tends to be less stable than a single-party majority government as disagreements between partners can cause the coalition to collapse. India has frequently had coalition governments at the Centre, such as the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) and the National Democratic Alliance (NDA).

अभिकथन (A) : कृषि उत्पादन से संबंधित क्रियाओं को तृतीयक क्षेत्रक में सम्मिलित किया जाता है।
कारण (R) : तृतीयक क्षेत्रक को सेवा क्षेत्रक कहा जाता है।
questions.text_english:
Two statements labelled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given below. Read both the statements carefully and choose the correct option :
Assertion (A) : Agricultural production related activities are included in the tertiary sector.
Reason (R) : Tertiary sector is called as service sector.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परंतु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true. Agricultural production activities belong to the Primary sector, not the Tertiary sector. The primary sector includes agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining, and related activities that directly use natural resources. The Tertiary sector (Reason R) is correctly called the service sector and includes banking, transport, trade, education, healthcare, and communication. Since Assertion A wrongly places agricultural activities in the tertiary sector, it is false. But the Reason that the tertiary sector is the service sector is indeed correct. Hence option D is the right answer.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन (A) गलत है क्योंकि कृषि उत्पादन प्राथमिक क्षेत्रक में आता है, तृतीयक में नहीं। कारण (R) सही है — तृतीयक क्षेत्रक को सेवा क्षेत्रक कहा जाता है। इसलिए विकल्प D सही है।

questions.text: वैश्वीकरण के संदर्भ में कुछ देश आयातित वस्तुओं पर शुल्क क्यों लगाते हैं ? निम्नलिखित विकल्पों में से सही कारण का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english: Why do some countries impose tariffs on imported goods in the context of globalization ? Choose the correct reason from the following options :

options.A: मुक्त व्यापार का समर्थन करने के लिए
options.B: स्थानीय उद्योगों की रक्षा करने के लिए
options.D: आयात लागत कम करने के लिए

questions.solution: Countries impose tariffs on imported goods to protect local industries from foreign competition. When cheaper foreign goods flood the market, domestic producers may not be able to compete, leading to job losses and the collapse of local industries. By imposing tariffs (import duties), the government makes foreign goods more expensive, giving domestic producers a price advantage. This is called trade protectionism. Option A is wrong because tariffs restrict free trade. Option C is incorrect as tariffs do not attract investment. Option D is wrong as tariffs actually increase import costs rather than lower them.
questions.solution_hindi: कुछ देश स्थानीय उद्योगों की रक्षा के लिए आयातित वस्तुओं पर शुल्क लगाते हैं। इससे विदेशी सस्ती वस्तुओं से घरेलू उद्योगों को प्रतिस्पर्धा का सामना नहीं करना पड़ता और रोजगार सुरक्षित रहते हैं।

questions.text: भारत में विनिमय के माध्यम के रूप में रुपए को ही स्वीकार क्यों किया जाता है ?
questions.text_english: Why is Rupee accepted as a medium of exchange in India ?

options.A: क्योंकि इसे भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक द्वारा राज्य सरकार की ओर से जारी किया जाता है।
options.B: क्योंकि इसे भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक द्वारा केंद्र सरकार की ओर से जारी किया जाता है।
options.C: क्योंकि इसे भारतीय स्टेट बैंक द्वारा केंद्र सरकार की ओर से जारी किया जाता है।
options.D: क्योंकि इसे भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक द्वारा विश्व बैंक की ओर से जारी किया जाता है।

options_english.A: Because it is issued by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the State Government.
options_english.B: Because it is issued by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the Central Government.
options_english.C: Because it is issued by the State Bank of India on behalf of the Central Government.
options_english.D: Because it is issued by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the World Bank.

questions.solution: The Rupee is accepted as a medium of exchange in India because it is issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on behalf of the Central Government of India. The Indian government has authorised the Rupee as legal tender, which means it must be accepted for payment of debts and transactions. The RBI, as the central bank, has the sole authority to issue currency notes in India. Options A, C, and D are incorrect — the State Government, State Bank of India, and World Bank have no role in issuing Indian currency.
questions.solution_hindi: भारत में रुपए को भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक द्वारा केंद्र सरकार की ओर से जारी किया जाता है इसीलिए इसे विनिमय के माध्यम के रूप में स्वीकार किया जाता है। यह सरकार द्वारा अधिकृत विधिग्राह्य मुद्रा है।

questions.text_english: Which of the following is an example of public sector ?
questions.solution: Indian Railways is an example of the public sector as it is owned and operated by the Government of India. In the public sector, the government owns the assets and provides services. Birla Cement, Tata Iron and Steel Company, and Reliance Industries Limited are all private sector companies owned by private individuals and corporations, not the government. Indian Railways is the largest public sector employer in India and provides essential transport services across the country under government management.

questions.text: श्रीमती दीप्ती X देश की निवासी हैं। उनका देश एक विकसित देश है। उसके देश की निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी एक विशेषता होगी ?
questions.text_english: Smt. Deepti is a resident of X country. Her country is a developed country. Which of the following would be a characteristic of her country ?
questions.solution: High per capita income is a characteristic of a developed country. Developed countries have high standards of living, high per capita income, advanced infrastructure, high literacy rates, low infant mortality rates, and high net enrolment ratios in schools. Options A, C, and D — high infant mortality rate, low literacy rate, and low net attendance ratio — are all features of developing or underdeveloped countries. Therefore, option B is the correct characteristic of a developed country.

questions.text: ऋण लेने में समर्थक ऋणाधार का उद्देश्य निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा एक है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following is the purpose of collateral in a loan ?

options.B: ऋणदाता के लिए ऋण सुरक्षित करना
options.C: ऋणदाता के लिए कागजी दस्तावेज़ कम करना

options_english.A: To increase the interest for the lender
options_english.B: To secure the loan for the lender
options_english.C: To reduce paperwork for the lender
options_english.D: To avoid repayment on the loan

questions.solution: The purpose of collateral in a loan is to secure the loan for the lender. Collateral is an asset (such as land, property, gold, or fixed deposits) that a borrower pledges to the lender as security. If the borrower fails to repay the loan, the lender has the right to sell the collateral to recover the money. This reduces the risk for the lender. It does not increase interest (A), reduce paperwork (C), or help the borrower avoid repayment (D). Hence option B is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: ऋणाधार (Collateral) का उद्देश्य ऋणदाता के लिए ऋण को सुरक्षित करना है। यदि उधारकर्ता ऋण नहीं चुकाता तो ऋणदाता ऋणाधार बेचकर अपना पैसा वापस ले सकता है।

questions.text: 'प्रच्छन्न बेरोज़गारी' की उदाहरण सहित व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain 'Disguised Unemployment' with example.

key_points: Disguised unemployment is when more people are employed than are actually needed for a job
Common in agriculture — if five people do work that can be done by two, three are disguisedly unemployed

questions.solution: Disguised unemployment is a situation where more people are engaged in a job than the number actually required to do that work. The extra workers appear to be employed but their marginal productivity is zero — removing them would not reduce the total output. This type of unemployment is very common in agriculture in India. For example, if a piece of land can be effectively cultivated by three people but five family members are working on it, the extra two are disguisedly unemployed. Their contribution to output is nil, and they would not be missed if they moved to another occupation.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रच्छन्न बेरोज़गारी वह स्थिति है जब किसी काम में आवश्यकता से अधिक लोग लगे हों। उनकी सीमांत उत्पादकता शून्य होती है। उदाहरण: यदि एक खेत पर 3 लोग काम कर सकते हैं लेकिन 5 काम करते हैं तो 2 प्रच्छन्न बेरोज़गार हैं।

questions.text: असंगठित क्षेत्रक में श्रमिकों के संरक्षण हेतु कोई तीन उपाय सुझाइए।
questions.text_english: Suggest any three measures for labour safety in the unorganised sector.

key_points: Government should enforce minimum wage laws for unorganised sector workers
Social security schemes like MGNREGS should be extended to protect workers
Workers should be provided with job security and regulated working hours

questions.solution: Three measures to protect workers in the unorganised sector are: First, the government must strictly implement and enforce minimum wage laws to ensure that workers are paid a fair wage and not exploited by employers. Second, government social security schemes such as the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGS) should be strengthened and their coverage expanded so that unorganised sector workers have a safety net during periods of unemployment. Third, unorganised sector workers should be provided with regulated working hours, protection from arbitrary dismissal, and access to basic facilities like provident fund, health insurance, and maternity benefits, similar to those enjoyed by workers in the organised sector.
questions.solution_hindi: असंगठित क्षेत्रक श्रमिकों की सुरक्षा के तीन उपाय: पहला, न्यूनतम मजदूरी कानून का कड़ाई से पालन हो। दूसरा, मनरेगा जैसी सामाजिक सुरक्षा योजनाओं का विस्तार किया जाए। तीसरा, कार्य के घंटे नियमित किए जाएँ और स्वास्थ्य बीमा जैसी सुविधाएँ दी जाएँ।

questions.text: 'शरीर द्रव्यमान सूचकांक' को परिभाषित कीजिए। इसकी गणना करने की विधि की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Define the term 'Body Mass Index'. Explain the method of its calculation.

key_points: BMI is a measure to assess whether a person is undernourished or overnourished
BMI = Weight in kg / (Height in metres)²
BMI below 18.5 indicates undernourishment; above 25 indicates overweight

questions.solution: Body Mass Index (BMI) is a measure used to assess the nutritional status of a person — whether they are undernourished, healthy, or overweight. It is used in healthcare and development studies as a human development indicator. The method of calculating BMI is: BMI = Weight of the person in kilograms ÷ (Height of the person in metres)². For example, if a person weighs 60 kg and is 1.65 metres tall, BMI = 60 ÷ (1.65)² = 60 ÷ 2.72 ≈ 22.06. A BMI below 18.5 indicates that the person is underweight or undernourished, a BMI between 18.5 and 24.9 is considered normal or healthy, and a BMI of 25 or above indicates overweight or obesity.
questions.solution_hindi: शरीर द्रव्यमान सूचकांक (BMI) किसी व्यक्ति के पोषण स्तर को मापने का एक तरीका है। गणना: BMI = वजन (किग्रा) ÷ (ऊँचाई मीटर में)²। 18.5 से कम BMI कुपोषण दर्शाता है, जबकि 25 से अधिक अधिक वजन दर्शाता है।

sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between the formal and informal sources of credit.

key_points: Formal sources: banks, cooperative societies — regulated by RBI
Informal sources: moneylenders, landlords, friends — no regulation
Formal sources charge lower interest rates
Informal sources charge high, exploitative interest rates
Formal sources require collateral; informal sources may not but exploit borrowers

sub_questions.solution: Formal and informal sources of credit differ significantly in terms of regulation, interest rates, and accessibility. Formal sources of credit include commercial banks, cooperative banks, and cooperative credit societies. These are registered with and regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), which monitors their functioning. They charge relatively lower and standardised interest rates. They require collateral and documentation for granting loans. Informal sources include moneylenders, landlords, traders, relatives, and friends. These are not regulated by any government body. They charge very high and often exploitative interest rates, leading borrowers into a debt trap. While they are more accessible in rural areas and require less documentation, their exploitative nature harms borrowers. The government aims to increase access to formal credit, especially in rural areas, to reduce dependence on informal lenders.

sub_questions.text: 'स्वयं-सहायता समूहों' की कार्यप्रणाली को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the functioning of 'Self-Help Groups'.

key_points: SHGs are small groups of 15–20 poor people, mostly women, who save regularly
Members borrow from the common pool at reasonable interest rates
After regular savings, SHGs become eligible for bank loans
They help members become self-reliant and free from moneylenders
Grameen Bank of Bangladesh is a successful model

sub_questions.solution: Self-Help Groups (SHGs) are small, informal groups of 15 to 20 members, mostly poor rural women, who come together to save regularly and support each other financially. Each member saves a small amount (as little as Rs 25 to Rs 100 per month) and the pooled savings form a common fund. Members can borrow from this fund at reasonable interest rates to meet emergencies or livelihood needs. Decisions about loans — how much to lend, to whom, and at what interest rate — are taken democratically by the group members themselves. After a track record of regular savings and repayments, the SHG becomes eligible for a bank loan in the group's name. This system provides rural poor, especially women, access to affordable credit without collateral, helps them start small businesses, and frees them from exploitative moneylenders. The Grameen Bank model in Bangladesh inspired the SHG movement in India.
